top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) combine a clear conceptual advance (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) with a reproduced 10^-18 realization used in geodesy, constant bounds and the second's redefinition. It is the only slate entry with a two-name allocation that members from every camp describe identically, and a citation limited to the lattice idea and its realization keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The Higgs discovery is the larger result and I rank it next, with Gianotti, Della Negra and Jenni preferred over the Virdee variant because it matches the trio I proposed at opening, but the three-of-four attribution remains a judgement call.
